notes.meaning: The Holy Spirit prompted Simeon to go into the temple courts at the exact hour Mary and Joseph arrived with baby Jesus. The parents had come to obey the law of Moses by dedicating their firstborn son to God. God arranged this divine meeting so Simeon could see the promised Savior with his own eyes.

Simeon scooped the infant Jesus into his arms and praised God with overwhelming joy. Holding this baby was the fulfillment of God's personal promise that he would not die before seeing the Messiah. We can praise God when we see His promises come true.

Simeon addressed God as his Master and asked to be released from earthly life in quiet trust. Because God kept His promise to show him the Messiah, Simeon felt his life's purpose was fulfilled. He was now ready to die in peace without any fear.

Simeon recognized that this tiny, helpless infant was God's rescue plan in human form. Seeing Jesus with his own eyes rewarded his long years of patient faith. Those who welcome Christ can face death with comfort and peace.

God prepared His plan of salvation openly for the whole world to see, like a great feast spread out for all nations. Jesus came to bring spiritual light and truth to the Gentiles, people outside the Jewish nation who had lived in spiritual darkness. At the same time, He came to be the greatest glory and honor of God's people, Israel.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Simeon's canticle is sung at every evening Vespers service, celebrating the meeting of the Old and New Covenants.

notes.meaning: Joseph and Mary were filled with wonder as they listened to Simeon speak about the baby's worldwide mission. Even though angels had already spoken to them, they continued to marvel as God revealed more about their child's calling. Believers can keep growing in their awe of who Jesus is.

Simeon blessed the family and warned Mary that Jesus would divide the people of Israel. Some who are proud would reject Him and fall into ruin, while others who are humble would be raised to life and forgiveness. He would also become a sign from God that many people would fiercely oppose.

differ.view: God ordained Christ as a stumbling block over whom the reprobate fall, while the elect are given faith to rise.

notes.meaning: How people respond to Jesus lays bare the secret desires and true condition of their hearts. Simeon also warned Mary that she would suffer intense personal grief, like a sharp sword piercing her soul, when watching her Son suffer and die. God forewarns His people to prepare them for difficult trials.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: The prophecy of the sword points ahead to the cross, where Mary as the Mother of God shares intimately in the suffering of her crucified Son.

notes.meaning: Anna was an elderly prophetess who had lost her husband after only seven years of marriage and lived as a widow to a very old age. She devoted her life entirely to God by remaining at the temple day and night, praying and fasting regularly. Her quiet faithfulness shows how valuable lifelong devotion is to God.

Anna walked up at that exact moment and began publicly thanking God for the infant Savior. She then went and told the good news to the small group of faithful believers who were waiting for God to redeem Jerusalem. Those who know Jesus should gladly tell others about Him.

After Mary and Joseph carefully obeyed every command required by God's law, they returned home to Nazareth in Galilee. Luke leaves out their escape to Egypt and later return, focusing on the fact that Jesus grew up in an ordinary, humble town. Jesus' family set a consistent example of obeying God's commands.

Jesus experienced a genuine human childhood, growing physically in body and maturing in mind. Unlike other children who are born with sinful hearts, He was filled with divine wisdom and lived continually under God's favor. His perfect childhood shows us what a life pleasing to God truly looks like.

Joseph and Mary traveled about seventy miles to Jerusalem every year to observe the Passover, the annual feast remembering Israel's deliverance from Egypt. When Jesus turned twelve, the age when Jewish boys were trained in adult duties under the law, He traveled with them to take part in the feast. Faithful parents make regular public worship a priority for their families.

When the festival days were finished, the family started home, but the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem without His parents knowing. He did not remain behind out of rebellion, but because He was completely absorbed in the things of God. His parents did not notice right away because they trusted His character.

Pilgrims traveled in large caravans of neighbors and extended family, so Mary and Joseph naturally thought Jesus was walking with friends. After a full day of travel, they searched the groups and realized He was missing, so they hurried back to Jerusalem to search for Him. When we realize we have lost our closeness with Christ, we should seek Him without delay.

On the third day of their journey and search, His parents discovered Jesus in the temple courts sitting among the religious teachers. He was listening respectfully, asking thoughtful questions about God's law, and giving answers that astonished the scholars. Young people can follow Jesus by showing respect to their elders while eagerly seeking spiritual knowledge.

Mary and Joseph were shocked to see their twelve-year-old son sitting among the most famous teachers of the nation. Mary expressed the deep distress they had suffered during the three-day search, asking why He had caused them so much pain. Even faithful believers can experience profound anxiety in confusing circumstances.

Jesus gently asked why they had searched all over for Him, reminding them that He had to be devoted to His heavenly Father. In these first recorded words of His life, Jesus showed that He understood His unique identity as God's Son. Our commitment to God must come before every other duty in life.

Joseph and Mary did not grasp what Jesus meant by His response. Even though they knew He was the promised Savior, they did not yet understand how His divine calling would take precedence over ordinary family life. Believers must patiently trust God when His plans are beyond their understanding.

Jesus returned to Nazareth with His parents and faithfully obeyed them during all the years He grew into manhood. Mary treasured each of these events and words deep in her heart, pondering their hidden meaning over time. Children can follow Christ's example by honoring and obeying their parents.

Jesus continued to grow physically in body, and His human soul developed in spiritual understanding and wisdom. His pure and unselfish life pleased God completely and earned the respect and love of the people around Him. True spiritual growth brings honor to God and blesses the community.
